title: SSC CGL — Combined: General Awareness + English Language

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of the Mauryan Empire in ancient India?

options.explanation: Ashoka was the grandson of Chandragupta Maurya and a later ruler of the Mauryan Empire.
Bindusara was the son of Chandragupta Maurya and the father of Ashoka.
Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan Empire in 322 BCE.
Samudragupta was a ruler of the Gupta Empire, not the Mauryan Empire.

questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya, with the guidance of Chanakya (Kautilya), overthrew the Nanda dynasty and established the Mauryan Empire around 322 BCE.
questions.hint: He was the grandfather of Ashoka.
questions.subject: ssc-gk

questions.question: The famous Battle of Plassey, a pivotal event in the history of British India, was fought in which year?

options.explanation: The Battle of Buxar was fought in 1764.
The Battle of Plassey was fought in 1757.
The Regulating Act was passed in 1773.
The Third Battle of Panipat was fought in 1761.

questions.explanation: The Battle of Plassey was fought on June 23, 1757, between the forces of the British East India Company, led by Robert Clive, and the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-Daulah.
questions.hint: It marked the beginning of British political dominance in India.
questions.subject: ssc-gk

questions.question: Which Sultan of Delhi Sultanate introduced the 'Dagh' (branding of horses) and 'Chehra' (descriptive roll of soldiers) systems to prevent corruption and ensure efficiency in the army?

options.explanation: Iltutmish was a Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate but did not introduce these systems.
Balban was known for his administrative reforms but not these specific systems.
Alauddin Khalji introduced the 'Dagh' and 'Chehra' systems.
Muhammad bin Tughlaq introduced other reforms but not these systems.

questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji implemented the 'Dagh' and 'Chehra' systems to maintain a strong and disciplined army, preventing soldiers from presenting inferior horses or substitutes during reviews and ensuring the exact identity of each soldier.
questions.hint: He was known for his military reforms and expansionist policies.
questions.subject: ssc-gk

questions.question: The ancient site of 'Kalibangan', known for its evidence of plough fields and fire altars from the Harappan Civilisation, is located in which Indian state?

options.explanation: Gujarat is home to other Harappan sites like Lothal and Dholavira.
Haryana has sites like Banawali but not Kalibangan.
Punjab has sites like Ropar but not Kalibangan.
Kalibangan is located in Rajasthan.

questions.explanation: Kalibangan is a significant archaeological site of the Indus Valley Civilization located in the Hanumangarh district of Rajasthan, India.
questions.hint: It is one of the major sites of the Indus Valley Civilization in India.
questions.subject: ssc-gk

questions.question: Who among the following was NOT associated with the 'Young Bengal Movement' in the 19th century?

options.explanation: Derozio was the leader of the Young Bengal Movement.
Ramtanu Lahiri was a member of the Young Bengal Movement.
Rasik Krishna Mallick was associated with the Young Bengal Movement.
Vidyasagar was not part of the Young Bengal Movement.

questions.explanation: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was a prominent social reformer and educationist but was not directly associated with the Young Bengal Movement.
questions.hint: The movement was led by Henry Louis Vivian Derozio.
questions.subject: ssc-gk

questions.question: The famous rock-cut caves of Elephanta, known for their Shiva iconography, were primarily built during the reign of which dynasty?

options.explanation: The Chalukyas were known for their rock-cut temples but not the Elephanta Caves.
The Pallavas were known for their rock-cut temples in Mahabalipuram.
The Rashtrakutas built the Elephanta Caves.
The Guptas were known for their art but not the Elephanta Caves.

questions.explanation: The Elephanta Caves, particularly the magnificent cave dedicated to Lord Shiva, are believed to have been primarily sculpted during the reign of the Rashtrakuta dynasty, between the 6th and 8th centuries CE.
questions.hint: The Rashtrakutas were known for their patronage of art and architecture.
questions.subject: ssc-gk

questions.question: Which of the following books was written by Harshavardhana, the Pushyabhuti ruler of Kannauj?

options.explanation: Kadambari was written by Banabhatta.
Harshacharita was written by Banabhatta.
Priyadarshika was written by Harshavardhana.
Ashtadhyayi was written by Panini.

questions.explanation: Harshavardhana himself was a skilled playwright and is credited with writing three Sanskrit plays: Priyadarshika, Ratnavali, and Nagananda. Kadambari and Harshacharita were written by Banabhatta, his court poet.
questions.hint: Harshavardhana was a patron of literature and wrote plays in Sanskrit.
questions.subject: ssc-gk

questions.question: The 'Poona Pact' was signed in 1932 between Mahatma Gandhi and which prominent leader, addressing the issue of separate electorates for depressed classes?

options.explanation: Nehru was not directly involved in the Poona Pact.
Patel was not part of the Poona Pact negotiations.
Ambedkar signed the Poona Pact with Gandhi.
Jinnah was not involved in the Poona Pact.

questions.explanation: The Poona Pact was an agreement signed on September 24, 1932, between Mahatma Gandhi and B.R. Ambedkar. It was a compromise that reserved seats for the depressed classes in the provincial and central legislatures.
questions.hint: He was a prominent leader of the Dalit community.
questions.subject: ssc-gk

questions.question: Who founded the Mauryan Empire in ancient India, overthrowing the Nanda dynasty?

options.explanation: Ashoka was the grandson of Chandragupta Maurya and a later emperor of the Mauryan dynasty.
Bindusara was the son of Chandragupta Maurya and father of Ashoka.
Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan Empire after overthrowing the Nanda dynasty.
Chanakya was the mentor and advisor to Chandragupta Maurya, not the founder of the empire.

questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya, with the help of his mentor Chanakya (Kautilya), founded the Mauryan Empire around 322 BCE after defeating the Nanda dynasty. Ashoka and Bindusara were later emperors of the same dynasty.
questions.hint: He was the grandfather of Ashoka.
questions.subject: ssc-gk

questions.question: The Great Bath, one of the most well-known structures of the Indus Valley Civilization, is found at which Harappan site?

options.explanation: Lothal is a Harappan site known for its dockyard and trade connections.
Kalibangan is known for its ploughed field and fire altars.
The Great Bath is located at Mohenjo-Daro, a major Harappan site.
Harappa is another significant Harappan site but does not contain the Great Bath.

questions.explanation: The Great Bath is a prominent structure discovered during the excavations at Mohenjo-Daro, indicating advanced civic planning and possibly ritualistic practices. Lothal, Kalibangan, and Harappa are other significant Harappan sites.
questions.hint: This site is located in present-day Pakistan.
questions.subject: ssc-gk

questions.question: The famous Sanskrit play 'Mudrarakshasa', which describes the ascent of Chandragupta Maurya to power, was authored by whom?

options.explanation: Kalidasa was a renowned poet and playwright known for works like 'Shakuntala' and 'Meghaduta'.
Vishakhadatta authored 'Mudrarakshasa', a play about Chandragupta Maurya's rise to power.
Bhasa was an ancient Indian playwright known for his plays like 'Pancharatra' and 'Dutavakyam'.
Sudraka was the author of 'Mrichchhakatika', a famous Sanskrit play.

questions.explanation: 'Mudrarakshasa' is a historical play written by Vishakhadatta, detailing the political intrigues involved in Chandragupta Maurya's rise. Kalidasa, Bhasa, and Sudraka were other renowned ancient Indian playwrights, but not the author of Mudrarakshasa.
questions.hint: The author's name is similar to a famous Sanskrit scholar.
questions.subject: ssc-gk

questions.question: Which Mughal emperor introduced the 'Din-i Ilahi', a syncretic religion aimed at combining the best elements of various religions, in 1582 AD?

options.explanation: Humayun was Akbar's father and ruled before him.
Shah Jahan was Akbar's grandson and built the Taj Mahal.
Akbar introduced Din-i Ilahi in 1582 AD.
Aurangzeb was Akbar's great-grandson and ruled much later.

questions.explanation: Emperor Akbar, known for his policy of religious tolerance, introduced Din-i Ilahi (Divine Faith) in 1582 AD. It was not a religion in the traditional sense but rather a spiritual path for his close associates.
questions.hint: He is often referred to as 'Akbar the Great'.
questions.subject: ssc-gk

questions.question: In the Gupta administration, the term 'Uparika' typically referred to which official position?

options.explanation: The chief of the army was typically referred to as 'Senapati'.
'Uparika' was the term used for provincial governors in the Gupta administration.
Village headmen were usually referred to as 'Gramika' or 'Mukhiya'.
The royal treasurer was typically known as 'Samaharta'.

questions.explanation: During the Gupta period, the empire was divided into provinces (Bhuktis), which were administered by officers known as 'Uparikas' or 'Uparika Maharajs'. They were often appointed directly by the emperor.
questions.hint: This position was responsible for managing provinces.
questions.subject: ssc-gk

questions.question: The Treaty of Srirangapatnam, which brought an end to the Third Anglo-Mysore War, was signed in which year?

options.explanation: The Treaty of Mangalore was signed in 1784, ending the Second Anglo-Mysore War.
The Treaty of Srirangapatnam was signed in 1792, ending the Third Anglo-Mysore War.
1799 was the year of the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War, which ended with Tipu Sultan's death.
1801 is not associated with any major Anglo-Mysore treaty.

questions.explanation: The Third Anglo-Mysore War concluded with the Treaty of Srirangapatnam in 1792, signed between Tipu Sultan and the British East India Company, along with its allies (Nizam of Hyderabad and Maratha Empire). 1784 saw the Treaty of Mangalore (Second Anglo-Mysore War) and 1799 was the year of the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.
questions.hint: This treaty ended the war that took place between 1789 and 1792.
questions.subject: ssc-gk

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Satavahana dynasty, which ruled parts of the Deccan region of India for several centuries?

options.explanation: Gautamiputra Satakarni was a later powerful ruler of the Satavahana dynasty.
Simuka is traditionally considered the founder of the Satavahana dynasty.
Hala was a celebrated poet-king of the Satavahana dynasty.
Vashishtiputra Pulumavi was another powerful ruler of the Satavahana dynasty.

questions.explanation: Simuka is traditionally considered the founder of the Satavahana dynasty, establishing their rule around the 3rd century BCE. Gautamiputra Satakarni and Vashishtiputra Pulumavi were later powerful rulers of the dynasty, while Hala was a celebrated poet-king.
questions.hint: His name is similar to a famous ancient Indian poet.
questions.subject: ssc-gk

questions.question: The 'Panchayatana' style of temple architecture, characterized by a main shrine and four subsidiary shrines at the corners, is a prominent feature that emerged during which period?

options.explanation: The Mauryan period is known for rock-cut architecture like the Barabar Caves.
The Panchayatana style emerged during the Gupta period, with the Dashavatara Temple at Deogarh as a prime example.
The Pala period is known for Buddhist monastic structures like the Somapura Mahavihara.
The Chola period is known for grand Dravidian style temples like the Brihadeeswarar Temple.

questions.explanation: The Panchayatana style, symbolizing a cosmic mandala, is a distinctive feature of Hindu temple architecture that began to develop during the Gupta period. A prime example is the Dashavatara Temple at Deogarh. The Mauryan period is known for rock-cut architecture, Pala for Buddhist monastic structures, and Chola for grand Dravidian style temples.
questions.hint: This period is often called the 'Golden Age of India'.
questions.subject: ssc-gk

questions.question: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose 'No Error'. Neither the students (A)/ or the teacher (B)/ was present (C)/ at the annual function. (D)/ No Error (E)

options.explanation: Part (A) is correct as it starts the correlative conjunction pair 'neither...'.
Part (B) contains the error. 'Or' should be replaced with 'nor' to pair with 'neither'.
Part (C) is correct as the verb 'was' agrees with the subject 'teacher'.
Part (D) is correct as it completes the sentence without error.

questions.explanation: The correlative conjunction pair 'neither...nor' is used. In part (B), 'or' should be replaced with 'nor' to form the correct pair with 'neither'. The verb 'was' agrees with the subject closer to it, 'teacher'.
questions.hint: Check the correlative conjunctions used in the sentence.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate conjunction: He is intelligent ____ he is also very hardworking.

options.explanation: 'But' indicates contrast, which is not suitable here.
'And' correctly joins the two positive attributes.
'So' indicates a result, which is not the intended meaning here.
'Although' indicates contrast, which is not suitable here.

questions.explanation: The sentence presents two positive attributes of the person. 'And' is used to join two similar or additive ideas.
questions.hint: Look for a conjunction that connects two positive statements.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose 'No Error'. Although he was tired, (A)/ yet he continued (B)/ to work on the project. (C)/ No Error (D)

options.explanation: Part (A) is correct as it starts the clause with 'Although'.
Part (B) contains the error. 'Yet' is redundant after 'Although'.
Part (C) is correct as it completes the sentence without error.
There is an error in the sentence, so 'No Error' is incorrect.

questions.explanation: The conjunction 'although' already implies a contrast. Using 'yet' after 'although' is redundant and grammatically incorrect.
questions.hint: Check for the use of redundant conjunctions.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose 'No Error'. No sooner did the bell ring (A)/ when the students (B)/ rushed out of the classroom. (C)/ No Error (D)

options.explanation: Part (A) is correct as it starts the clause with 'No sooner'.
Part (B) contains the error. 'When' should be replaced with 'than'.
Part (C) is correct as it completes the sentence without error.
There is an error in the sentence, so 'No Error' is incorrect.

questions.explanation: The correct correlative conjunction pair for 'no sooner' is 'than'. Therefore, 'when' in part (B) should be replaced with 'than'.
questions.hint: Check the correlative conjunctions used with 'no sooner'.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate conjunction: You will not understand the concept ____ you pay close attention.

options.explanation: 'Unless' correctly introduces the conditional meaning.
'If' does not convey the negative conditional meaning required here.
'Provided' indicates a condition but does not fit the negative context.
'Whether' introduces a choice, which is not suitable here.

questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if not'. The sentence implies that understanding will not happen if close attention is not paid.
questions.hint: Look for a conjunction that introduces a conditional meaning.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose 'No Error'. He is not only (A)/ a good singer but also (B)/ plays the guitar well. (C)/ No Error (D)

options.explanation: Part (A) is correct as it starts the correlative conjunction pair 'not only'.
Part (B) is correct as it completes the correlative conjunction pair 'but also'.
Part (C) contains the error. It should be 'a good guitarist' to maintain parallelism with 'a good singer'.
There is an error in the sentence, so 'No Error' is incorrect.

questions.explanation: For the correlative conjunction 'not only...but also', the structures following 'not only' and 'but also' must be parallel. Here, 'a good singer' (noun phrase) is followed by 'plays the guitar well' (verb phrase). To maintain parallelism, part (C) should be 'a good guitarist' (noun phrase).
questions.hint: Check for parallel structure in correlative conjunctions.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. If there is no error, choose 'No Error'. Walk carefully (A)/ lest you fall (B)/ down and hurt yourself. (C)/ No Error (D)

options.explanation: Part (A) is correct as it starts the sentence with an adverb.
Part (B) is correct as 'lest' is used appropriately here.
Part (C) is correct as it completes the sentence without error.
There is no error in the sentence.

questions.explanation: The conjunction 'lest' means 'for fear that'. It is used to introduce a clause expressing something feared or avoided. The sentence is grammatically correct as it stands.
questions.hint: Check the meaning and usage of 'lest'.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Identify the error in the sentence: 'Hardly had he reached the station than the train departed, leaving him stranded.'

options.text: Hardly had he reached the station
options.explanation: This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
This is the incorrect part. The correct conjunction is 'when', not 'than'.
This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
There is an error in the sentence.

questions.explanation: The correlative conjunction pair for 'Hardly' is 'when', not 'than'. The correct sentence should be: 'Hardly had he reached the station when the train departed.'
questions.hint: Correlative conjunctions must be used in pairs. 'Hardly' is paired with 'when'.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Identify the error in the sentence: 'Neither the manager or his subordinates were present at the meeting.'

options.explanation: This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
This is the incorrect part. The correct conjunction is 'nor', not 'or'.
This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
There is an error in the sentence.

questions.explanation: The correlative conjunction pair for 'Neither' is 'nor', not 'or'. The correct sentence should be: 'Neither the manager nor his subordinates were present at the meeting.'
questions.hint: Correlative conjunctions must be used in pairs. 'Neither' is paired with 'nor'.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Identify the error in the sentence: 'Walk carefully lest you should not fall down the stairs.'

options.explanation: This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
This is the incorrect part. 'Not' should not be used after 'lest'.
This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
There is an error in the sentence.

questions.explanation: The conjunction 'lest' itself implies a negative purpose ('for fear that'). Therefore, 'not' should not be used after 'lest' as it makes the sentence redundant. The correct sentence should be: 'Walk carefully lest you should fall down the stairs.'
questions.hint: 'Lest' already implies a negative meaning, so 'not' is redundant.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Identify the error in the sentence: 'Although he is wealthy, yet he is not content with his life.'

options.explanation: This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
This is the incorrect part. 'Yet' should be omitted for formal correctness.
This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
There is an error in the sentence.

questions.explanation: When 'Although' or 'Though' is used to begin a sentence, it is followed by a comma, but 'yet' is optional and often omitted. Using both 'Although' and 'yet' together is generally considered redundant in formal English. The correct sentence should be: 'Although he is wealthy, he is not content with his life.'
questions.hint: Using both 'Although' and 'yet' together is redundant.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Identify the error in the sentence: 'He is as good, if not better than his brother.'

options.explanation: This is the incorrect part. The phrase should be 'as good as'.
This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
There is an error in the sentence.

questions.explanation: When comparing two qualities where one is positive and the other comparative, the positive comparison must be complete. The phrase should be 'as good as'. The correct sentence should be: 'He is as good as, if not better than his brother.'
questions.hint: The phrase 'as good as' is required for correct comparison.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Identify the error in the sentence: 'No sooner did the bell ring when the students rushed out of the classroom.'

options.text: No sooner did the bell ring
options.explanation: This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
This is the incorrect part. The correct conjunction is 'than', not 'when'.
This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
There is an error in the sentence.

questions.explanation: The correlative conjunction pair for 'No sooner' is 'than', not 'when'. The correct sentence should be: 'No sooner did the bell ring than the students rushed out of the classroom.'
questions.hint: Correlative conjunctions must be used in pairs. 'No sooner' is paired with 'than'.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Identify the error in the sentence: 'It was such a hot day so we decided to stay indoors.'

options.text: It was such a hot day
options.explanation: This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
This is the incorrect part. The correct conjunction is 'that', not 'so'.
This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
There is an error in the sentence.

questions.explanation: The correct correlative conjunction pair to express cause and effect with 'such' is 'such...that'. 'So' is incorrect here. The correct sentence should be: 'It was such a hot day that we decided to stay indoors.'
questions.hint: The correct pair is 'such...that' for cause and effect.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Identify the error in the sentence: 'The teacher asked that if the students had completed their homework.'

options.explanation: This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
This is the incorrect part. 'That' should not be used before 'if'.
This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
There is an error in the sentence.

questions.explanation: In an indirect question, 'that' is not used before 'if' or 'whether'. Using both 'that' and 'if' creates redundancy. The correct sentence should be: 'The teacher asked if the students had completed their homework.'
questions.hint: 'That' is not used before 'if' in indirect questions.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Identify the error in the sentence: 'Both Ramesh as well as Suresh are responsible for this mistake.'

options.explanation: This is the incorrect part. The correct conjunction is 'and', not 'as well as'.
This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
There is an error in the sentence.

questions.explanation: The correct correlative conjunction pair for 'Both' is 'and', not 'as well as'. Using 'as well as' with 'Both' is redundant and grammatically incorrect. The correct sentence should be: 'Both Ramesh and Suresh are responsible for this mistake.'
questions.hint: The correct pair is 'Both...and'.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Identify the error in the sentence: 'Unless you don't work harder, you will not succeed.'

options.explanation: This is the incorrect part. 'Don't' should not be used after 'Unless'.
This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
There is an error in the sentence.

questions.explanation: The conjunction 'Unless' already means 'if not'. Therefore, using 'don't' after 'Unless' creates a double negative and is redundant. The correct sentence should be: 'Unless you work harder, you will not succeed.'
questions.hint: 'Unless' already implies a negative meaning, so 'don't' is redundant.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Identify the error in the sentence: 'Hardly had he reached the station then the train started and he missed it.'

options.text: Hardly had he reached the station
options.explanation: This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
This is the incorrect part of the sentence. It should be 'when the train started'.
This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
There is an error in the sentence.

questions.explanation: The correlative conjunction 'Hardly...when' is used to indicate that one event immediately followed another. The word 'then' is incorrectly used here. The correct conjunction to pair with 'Hardly' is 'when'.
questions.hint: The correct correlative conjunction pair for 'Hardly' is 'when'.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Identify the error in the sentence: 'Walk carefully lest you will fall and injure yourself.'

options.explanation: This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
This is the incorrect part of the sentence. It should be 'lest you should fall'.
This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
There is an error in the sentence.

questions.explanation: The conjunction 'lest' means 'for fear that' or 'in order to prevent something from happening'. It is always followed by 'should' and never by 'will' or 'would'.
questions.hint: The conjunction 'lest' should be followed by 'should'.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Identify the error in the sentence: 'Although he was tired but he continued to work late into the night.'

options.explanation: This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
This is the incorrect part of the sentence. The 'but' is redundant and should be removed.
This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
There is an error in the sentence.

questions.explanation: When a sentence begins with 'Although' or 'Though', it is incorrect to use 'but' or 'yet' in the main clause to introduce the contrasting idea. The conjunction 'although' itself is sufficient to convey the contrast.
questions.hint: Avoid using 'but' after 'Although'.
questions.subject: ssc-english
